elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer (no prohibition on developing, marketing, selling or acquiring competing products/services)
elements.evidence: 12.4 as revised: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."

elements.element: No field-of-use / territorial restriction on Customer
elements.evidence: 12.3 "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory"; 12.4 permission extends to "any territory"

elements.element: No post-term compete tail binding Customer
elements.evidence: the twenty-four month tail now attaches to a permission, not a prohibition: "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire"

elements.element: Restriction limited to a named competing product
elements.evidence: no product is named; the surviving text is a general permission covering "any product or service"

elements.element: Restriction limited to the term only
elements.evidence: text retains "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" (though now permissive)
"twenty-four months thereafter" remains in the sentence
no carve-out language; no restriction exists to carve out from
no acquisition carve-out; 12.4 instead permits acquiring competing products outright

reasons: The single operator flip ("shall not" to "may") in 12.4 removes the non-compete, field-of-use and territorial restraint on Customer, satisfying the locked preferred position that no non-compete or field-of-use restriction bind Customer.
Minimality is satisfied: one short phrase was replaced, no new exceptions, boilerplate or whole-clause rewrite, and 12.3's existing protections were left untouched.

Intent is preserved: the amended 12.4 is a permission consistent with 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer gave no non-compete commitment; no undefined term, contradiction or dangling mechanic is introduced (the residual "twenty-four months thereafter" merely extends a permission and is harmless to Customer).

Fallback elements (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, internal development and acquisition carve-outs) are absent, but that is expected and immaterial because the preferred level is fully met; the fallback is properly offered only in the non-operative margin comment.
